approved: The Imported Food Charges (Imposition-Customs) Bill 2015 was introduced as part of a four‑bill package, imposing charges only when they are considered a duty of customs, with the amounts and exemptions to be set in regulations.

The Imported Food Charges (Imposition-Excise) Bill 2015 was introduced as part of a legislative package to impose excise charges on imported food, with the amounts and exemptions to be set in delegated legislation rather than the bill itself.

The Imported Food Charges (Collection) Bill 2015 provides the authority to collect charges for imported food cost recovery, with regulations setting payment times, agent liability, and late fees. It includes non-payment measures such as suspending certificates and recovering debts, while allowing refunds at the Agriculture Secretary's discretion.

The speaker defended the Auditor-General's report on imported food inspection as generally effective, disagreed with the member for Hunter's criticism, and noted three recommendations are being implemented. They also announced four Imported Food Charges bills to enable cost-recovery for food safety activities and stated the government is consulting on simpler country-of-origin food labelling, with around 8,000 responses received.
